concepts.title: A lease is temporary ownership
concepts.explanation: Expiry permits recovery but does not prove the original worker stopped or that work happens exactly once.
concepts.quote: A lease grants one worker temporary ownership of a job until a recorded expiry.

concepts.title: An owner token fences stale completion
concepts.explanation: The current lease token must match before a result can be committed.
concepts.quote: Every completion checks that its token still matches the job's current lease.

concepts.title: An idempotency key names intent
concepts.explanation: A durable result store returns the same outcome for the same intended operation; meaningful inputs belong in the key.
concepts.quote: An idempotency key names one intended operation across retries.

concepts.title: A lease cannot promise exactly once
concepts.explanation: A lease limits overlap but repeated execution remains possible after timeout or crash.
concepts.quote: A lease reduces overlap, but it cannot prove exactly-once execution.

concepts.title: Protect the side-effect boundary
concepts.explanation: At-least-once work may repeat, so a lease alone cannot prove exactly-once execution.
concepts.quote: Put the idempotency check at the side-effect boundary, such as charging a card or publishing an artifact.

concepts.title: A receipt traces a released claim
concepts.explanation: Trace a claim through source, transformation, and delivered artifact while distinguishing assigned from unexamined ideas.
concepts.quote: An evidence receipt links a published claim to the exact source unit, the operation that transformed it, and the artifact users received.

concepts.title: Review content and delivery separately
concepts.explanation: A good script and a clean transcription each answer only part of the release question.
concepts.quote: Review the authored lesson and the delivered medium separately.

lessons.title: Recover a stalled job without trusting the clock
lessons.summary: A lease makes work reclaimable; a token makes stale completion harmless.

sections.heading: The clock opens a recovery path
sections.body: A worker claims a job for a limited time and renews its lease while it progresses. If renewal stops, another worker can try. Expiry changes who may claim the job, but it says nothing certain about whether the old worker is still running. The related retry source reaches the same limit from another angle: a lease reduces overlap but cannot promise exactly-once execution. Treat a timeout as uncertainty, not proof of death or nonexecution.

sections.heading: The token settles who may publish
sections.body: Give each lease a fresh owner token. At completion, compare the worker's token with the job's current token in the same commit step. If a replacement has already claimed the job, the old result cannot become the published result. A heartbeat helps operators see activity, but the token comparison enforces ownership.

questions.prompt: What does lease expiry permit, and what does it fail to prove?
questions.answer: It permits another claim; it does not prove the first worker stopped.
questions.rationale: The first worker may finish late, so recovery and safe publication are separate concerns.

questions.prompt: How do a heartbeat and an owner token solve different problems?
questions.answer: A heartbeat reports activity; a token check decides whether this attempt may commit.
questions.rationale: Observed liveness is useful information, while fencing is the actual publication rule.

questions.prompt: Worker A's lease expires, worker B claims the job, then A finishes. What should happen to A's result?
questions.answer: Reject it for publication because A's token no longer matches; retain it only for diagnosis if useful.
questions.rationale: Expiry did not stop A, so the completion path must check current ownership.

audio_script.text: A lease is a recovery tool. It lets another worker try after an expiry, but it cannot tell us that the first worker died.
Now add an owner token. If the first worker returns after a replacement has claimed the job, its token no longer matches. It may finish its calculation; it may not publish the result.
Pause and predict: a late worker finishes after its lease expired. Which check decides whether it may publish?
The current owner-token check. Remember the split: the clock opens recovery; the token protects the commit.

scenario.title: A worker returns after timeout
scenario.candidate_brief: A report job has stalled. Another worker is available. Describe a safe recovery plan.

findings.label: Lease record
findings.text: The recorded lease has expired; the original worker's process status is unknown.

findings.label: Publication state
findings.text: No final report has been published. The job has a current owner-token field.

scenario.decision_prompt: What can the replacement worker do now, and what must happen before either worker publishes?

checklist.criterion: Recognizes that expiry permits a new claim but does not prove the old worker stopped.
Requires a current owner-token match at completion.

second_event.text: The original worker finishes moments after the replacement claims the job.

scenario.reassessment_prompt: Should the original result become the published report? Explain the ownership check.
scenario.debrief: The replacement may claim after expiry. The original worker's late result must fail the current-token check; a heartbeat cannot substitute for this fence.

lessons.title: Make retries safe where effects happen
lessons.summary: Temporary ownership limits overlap; idempotency at the effect boundary makes repeated attempts safe.

sections.heading: Name one intended operation
sections.body: Use an idempotency key that represents the operation and all inputs that change its meaning. Record the completed outcome durably under that key. A retry with the same intent can read the prior outcome. If different inputs reuse the key, the store may return a result for the wrong operation, so key design is part of correctness.

sections.heading: Guard the irreversible step
sections.body: A crashed caller may have performed the effect before losing its reply, and a replacement may run the job again. A lease can reduce simultaneous work, yet repeated execution remains possible. Check idempotency at the effect itself: before charging, publishing, or sending. A cached draft or model answer is useful, but it is not evidence that the external effect committed once.

questions.prompt: What must an idempotency key represent?
questions.answer: One intended operation, including inputs that change its meaning.
questions.rationale: The store can safely return an earlier result only when the intent is truly the same.

questions.prompt: Why is a lease insufficient where an idempotency check is needed?
questions.answer: A lease limits ownership for a time, but a timed-out attempt can still finish and a job can execute twice; the idempotency check guards the side effect.
questions.rationale: Temporary ownership and repeated-effect control solve different failure modes.

questions.prompt: A payment service charged a card, then the caller timed out before seeing the reply. Where should the retry be checked?
questions.answer: At the charge boundary using the same intent key and its durable completed outcome.
questions.rationale: Caching the caller's earlier reasoning does not establish whether the card was charged.

audio_script.text: Last lesson, a lease and token controlled who could publish. Now consider an effect that may already have happened before a timeout.
An idempotency key names that intended operation. Store its outcome durably and use the same key on retry. Include the inputs that make the operation distinct.
Pause and compare: does a valid lease alone prove that a payment happened only once?
No. Put the duplicate check at the payment boundary. The lease helps coordinate workers; the idempotency key contains retries of the effect.

scenario.title: The payment reply vanished
scenario.candidate_brief: A customer retries a payment after the first request timed out. Decide what the workflow should do.

findings.label: Request identity
findings.text: Both requests have the same customer, order, amount, and intended operation.

findings.label: Worker history
findings.text: The first worker lost its reply. A replacement worker now owns the job lease.

scenario.decision_prompt: Where should the retry be checked, and what result should it return if the first charge completed?

checklist.criterion: Uses a key that represents the meaningful payment inputs.
Checks durable completion at the charge boundary and reuses the prior outcome.

second_event.text: The retry arrives with a different amount but the same supplied idempotency key.

scenario.reassessment_prompt: Would you return the old outcome for the changed amount? What identity error must be resolved?
scenario.debrief: A timeout is not proof that the charge failed. Check the durable effect under a key for the original intent; changed meaningful inputs require a distinct identity or an explicit conflict.

lessons.title: Release claims need evidence at every handoff
lessons.summary: Trace what was learned and delivered, then state what each check actually established.

sections.heading: Follow a claim to its source and artifact
sections.body: A release receipt connects a claim to the precise source unit, the transformation that produced it, and what the user received. Counts such as pages visited are process measures. They cannot prove that extraction found every important idea. Show which extracted ideas became lessons, which were deliberately deferred, and what was never evaluated.

sections.heading: Inspect meaning and medium
sections.body: Read the authored lesson for correctness and useful flow. Then inspect the delivered medium: a script can be clipped, muted, or misread in audio. The reverse is also true: transcription can agree perfectly with a confusing lesson. Say exactly which check passed and reopen the smallest stage that failed, rather than treating one green badge as proof of the whole product.

questions.prompt: What three links should an evidence receipt make inspectable?
questions.answer: The exact source unit, the transformation, and the delivered artifact.
questions.rationale: The receipt gives a reviewer a path from claim to evidence and user experience.

questions.prompt: What do page counts, script review, and delivery review each fail to prove?
questions.answer: Page counts do not prove complete comprehension; script review does not prove the delivered medium is intact; delivery review does not prove the lesson teaches well.
questions.rationale: Each measure addresses a different handoff and has a narrow scope.

questions.prompt: A generated audio lesson matches its transcript, but learners cannot explain the topic. Which stage would you inspect first?
questions.answer: Inspect the lesson plan and authored explanation for teaching quality, using source evidence; transcript agreement only checked delivery.
questions.rationale: A clean medium can faithfully deliver an unhelpful lesson.

audio_script.text: We now have recovery and safe retries. How do we know the released learning artifact actually deserves trust? Follow a claim from its source unit through the transformation to what the learner received.
A page count says pages were visited. It cannot say every important idea was understood. Separate assigned, deferred, and unexamined material.
Pause and apply: the transcript matches the audio, but the explanation is confusing. Which check passed, and what remains open?
Delivery agreement passed. Teaching quality remains open. Inspect the authored lesson and its evidence, then fix the smallest stage that created the confusion.

scenario.title: A green release badge is challenged
scenario.candidate_brief: A learning artifact is marked ready. A user reports that the lesson is confusing. Investigate the release claim.

findings.label: Processing receipt
findings.text: Every uploaded page was processed, and the published lesson has source-unit references.

findings.label: Delivery receipt
findings.text: A transcription agrees with the audio script, but no human read the full lesson for teaching flow.

scenario.decision_prompt: What do the receipts establish, and what would you inspect before claiming the artifact teaches well?

checklist.criterion: Distinguishes processed pages from complete extraction or teaching coverage.
Separately inspects authored lesson quality and delivered-medium quality.

second_event.text: A source unit contains a relevant exception absent from the extracted concept board.

scenario.reassessment_prompt: Which earliest handoff failed, and how should the coverage claim change?
scenario.debrief: The earliest loss is concept extraction, before planning or delivery. A green transcript check still says only that the medium matched the script; reopen extraction and state the narrower coverage claim.
